message:
Earlier you read the document below and made these notes on it:

<notes>
Fenbridge's household waste rules for 2026–27. The grey rubbish bin and the blue recycling bin (paper, card, cans, plastic bottles, pots, tubs and trays) are each collected fortnightly on alternate weeks, and the food caddy every week. Collections shift a day later after bank holidays. Bins must be at the property edge by 6.30 am with lids shut; late bins wait until the next collection. Side waste beside the grey bin isn't taken, apart from up to two extra bags in the two collections after Christmas, but extra recycling in a clear bag is always taken. The optional brown garden waste bin costs £52 a year (£46 by direct debit), is non-refundable, and is emptied every two weeks throughout the year. Bulky items cost £30 for up to three, £10 for each extra (max six), and £25 per fridge or freezer; book five working days ahead. Households that can't move bins due to disability or frailty can apply to Waste Services for an assisted collection. The council replaces lost, stolen or damaged grey, blue and brown bins free of charge, and food caddies too. Report a missed collection within five working days and the crew will return within three working days. Contaminated blue bins are tagged and left. Street waste outside collection times risks a £100 fixed penalty.
</notes>

Here is the document itself, for reference:

<document>
FENBRIDGE DISTRICT COUNCIL — HOUSEHOLD WASTE AND RECYCLING COLLECTIONS: RULES FOR RESIDENTS (2026–27)

1. What we collect and when. • Grey bin (general rubbish): collected every two weeks. • Blue bin (mixed recycling: paper, card, cans, plastic bottles, pots, tubs and trays): collected every two weeks, on the alternate week to the grey bin. • Food caddy (all food waste, in compostable liners): collected every week. • Brown bin (garden waste): optional paid service, see section 4. Your collection day is shown on the council website. Collections after a bank holiday move one day later for the rest of that week.

2. Putting your bins out. Bins must be at the edge of your property, next to the public highway, by 6.30 am on your collection day, with lids closed. Bins put out late will not be collected until the next scheduled collection. Please take bins back in by the end of the collection day.

3. Extra waste. We will only empty the waste inside your grey bin with the lid closed. Extra bags of rubbish left next to the grey bin ("side waste") will not be collected, except in the two collections immediately after Christmas Day, when up to two extra black bags will be taken. Extra recycling in a clear bag next to the blue bin will be collected at any time.

4. Garden waste. The brown bin service costs £52 per bin per year (April to March), or £46 if paid by direct debit. Brown bins are emptied every two weeks from March to November. There are no garden waste collections in December, January or February. Subscriptions are not refundable, and are not reduced for the winter suspension.

5. Bulky waste. We collect up to three bulky items (such as furniture or mattresses) for £30, and £10 for each additional item, up to a maximum of six items. Fridges and freezers are £25 each. Book online at least five working days before the collection.

6. Assisted collections. If no one in your household is able to move a bin to the kerb because of disability or frailty, you can apply for an assisted collection. Applications are assessed by the Waste Services team, who may visit. If approved, our crew will collect bins from an agreed point on your property and return them.

7. Damaged, lost and stolen bins. If your bin is damaged by our crew or the collection vehicle, we will replace or repair it free of charge. If your bin is lost or stolen, or damaged in any other way, you must pay £28 for a replacement grey, blue or brown bin, including delivery. Food caddies are replaced free.

8. Missed collections. If your bin was out on time but was not emptied, report it on the website within two working days of your collection day. We will return to empty it within three working days of the report. We cannot return for reports made after two working days; the bin will be emptied on the next scheduled collection.

9. Contamination. If your blue bin contains the wrong items, it will be tagged and not emptied. Remove the wrong items and it will be emptied on the next scheduled blue bin day.

10. Enforcement. Leaving waste on the street outside collection times may lead to a fixed penalty of up to £100 under the Environmental Protection Act 1990.
</document>

A few questions from someone who needs to act on this:
1. Will my brown garden waste bin be emptied in January?
2. Our blue recycling bin was stolen last week. Who pays for the replacement?
3. My grey bin was out on time on Monday but wasn't emptied. I'm reporting it on Thursday (three working days later). Will the council come back for it?
4. By what time must bins be put out on collection day?
response:
Answers below are from the document itself. My earlier notes got three of these points wrong, so ignore them where they differ.

**1. Will my brown garden waste bin be emptied in January?**
No. Brown bins are emptied every two weeks from March to November only. There are no garden waste collections in December, January or February. The subscription isn't reduced or refunded for the winter break (Section 4). *(My notes wrongly said it ran all year.)*

**2. Our blue bin was stolen. Who pays for the replacement?**
You do. A replacement grey, blue or brown bin for one that was lost or stolen costs **£28**, including delivery. The council only pays when its crew or collection vehicle damaged the bin. Food caddies are the only thing replaced free regardless (Section 7). *(My notes wrongly said all replacements were free.)*

**3. Grey bin missed Monday, reporting Thursday. Will they come back?**
No. You have to report a missed collection within **two working days** of your collection day, which for a Monday collection means by Wednesday. A Thursday report is too late. The council won't return, and the bin will be emptied on your next scheduled grey bin collection, which is two weeks away (Section 8). *(My notes wrongly said five working days.)* Since you can't put extra bags beside the grey bin (Section 3), you'll need to fit the extra rubbish into the bin with the lid closed.

**4. By what time must bins be put out?**
By **6.30 am** on collection day, at the edge of your property next to the public highway, with lids closed. Late bins won't be collected until the next scheduled collection (Section 2).
